citation: CMS IOM Pub. 100-04, Claims Processing Manual, Chapter 1, Section 80
title: Handling Incomplete or Invalid Claims (Unprocessable Claims)
scope: Original Medicare Fee-for-Service (Part A and Part B)
key_principle: Claims returned as unprocessable (with RARC MA130) lack initial determination appeal rights under SSA § 1869; resubmission as a clean claim is required.

title: Basic conditions for Medicare payment: Time limits for filing claims
scope: Original Medicare Fee-for-Service
key_principle: Claims must be filed within 1 calendar year from Date of Service. Statutory exceptions are strictly limited to: (1) Administrative error by CMS/MAC; (2) Retroactive entitlement; (3) Retroactive entitlement involving State Medicaid; (4) Retroactive disenrollment from Medicare Advantage.

title: Determinations; Appeals
scope: Medicare Initial Determinations & Administrative Review
key_principle: Establishes 5-level Medicare appeals process for initial determinations. Does not apply to claims returned as unprocessable prior to initial determination.

citation: Cigna HealthCare Claims Submission Guidelines & Appeals/Disputes Procedures
title: Claims Submission and Dispute Procedures
scope: Commercial Managed Care (HMO, PPO, POS, Open Access Plus)
key_principle: Original claim timely filing: 90 days par / 180 days non-par. Corrected claims via EDI Frequency Code 7 with original ICN (Loop 2300 REF*F8) governed by provider contract. Provider dispute/appeal: 180 days from initial EOP.

citation: CMS IOM Pub. 100-04, Claims Processing Manual, Chapter 1, Section 120
title: Duplicate Claims Processing
scope: Original Medicare Fee-for-Service
key_principle: Standardizes duplicate checking logic across line-item and claim-level submissions; exact duplicates are adjusted under CARC 18 without appeal rights unless billed as distinct services with qualifying modifiers.

title: Medicare as Secondary Payer (MSP)
scope: Medicare Secondary Payer Statutory Rules
key_principle: Federal statute establishing order of liability. Medicare is secondary to EGHP for Working Aged (20+ employees), Disability (100+ employees), and 30-month ESRD coordination period. Medicare is primary for small employers (<20 or <100 employees) or after ESRD coordination period.

title: Exclusions from Medicare and Limitations on Medicare Payment
scope: Medicare Secondary Payer Regulations
key_principle: Governs employer size thresholds, conditional payment authorization (§ 411.52), and recovery actions when primary non-Medicare payers fail to pay promptly.

citation: NAIC Coordination of Benefits Model Regulation (Model #120)
title: Coordination of Benefits Model Regulation
scope: Model Guidelines for State Commercial Insurance Regulation
key_principle: Establishes model priority rules (Subscriber vs Dependent, Birthday Rule, Active vs Retiree/COBRA) widely adopted by state insurance departments. Operates as model state guidance, subject to state statutory variations and ERISA self-funded plan terms.

title: Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA)
scope: Medicare-Participating Hospitals with Dedicated Emergency Departments
key_principle: Mandates hospitals to provide an appropriate medical screening examination and stabilizing treatment for emergency medical conditions regardless of ability to pay. Applies to hospital obligations, not as a universal health plan claims reimbursement override.

title: Preventing Surprise Medical Bills for Emergency Services
scope: Group Health Plans and Health Insurance Issuers
key_principle: Prohibits group health plans and health insurance issuers from requiring prior authorization for emergency services, and restricts beneficiary cost-sharing for out-of-network emergency care to in-network benefit levels.

title: 835 Compliance: Sending OA to Noncontracted Providers
scope: Electronic Remittance Advice (835) / Group Code OA
key_principle: Group Code OA does not provide clear direction on adjustment liability on its own; liability determination requires evaluating the group code, complete ERA, and original claim adjudication outcome under governing contracts and rules.

title: Certification of Medicare Supplemental Health Insurance Policies (Medigap)
scope: Medicare Supplement (Medigap) Insurance
key_principle: Medigap policies are standardized private supplemental insurance products specifically designed to cover Medicare cost-sharing; Medigap is strictly supplemental, always pays secondary to Medicare, and is never primary.

title: Medicare Secondary Payer: Current employment status
scope: Medicare Secondary Payer Regulations
key_principle: Statutory Medicare Secondary Payer working-aged provisions apply only to coverage based on current employment status; Medicare is legally primary over commercial retiree group health coverage.

citation: CMS Hospital Outpatient Department (OPD) Prior Authorization Program FAQs (Nov 14, 2024; Questions 28, 53–57; 42 CFR §§ 419.80–419.83)
title: Hospital Outpatient Department (OPD) Prior Authorization Frequently Asked Questions
scope: Original Medicare Fee-for-Service Hospital Outpatient Department (OPD) Services (Type of Bill 13X)
key_principle: If a hospital bypasses the prior authorization process, an ABN is not appropriate and the hospital may not charge the beneficiary (Q55). Under Q53, when prior authorization was requested and non-affirmed based on lack of medical necessity, the hospital must issue the Advance Beneficiary Notice of Noncoverage (ABN) to the beneficiary in advance and submit the claim appending modifier GA. Under Q57, for procedures ordinarily considered cosmetic that may be medically necessary for the patient's specific condition, the hospital must issue an advance ABN if denial is anticipated and submit the claim appending modifier GA. For statutorily excluded cosmetic services, issuing an ABN is voluntary, and the claim is submitted appending modifier GX (Q56).

citation: CMS IOM Pub. 100-04, Medicare Claims Processing Manual, Chapter 30, Section 50
title: Form CMS-R-131 Advance Beneficiary Notice of Noncoverage (ABN)
scope: Original Medicare Fee-for-Service (Part A and Part B)
key_principle: Issued to Medicare FFS beneficiaries before furnishing items or services when Medicare is expected to deny payment based on statutory benefit exclusions (e.g., medical necessity under SSA § 1862(a)(1)). An ABN is not a generic authorization waiver and cannot be used to bill beneficiaries when required prior authorization was bypassed.

title: No Surprises Act — Requirements for notice and consent for certain nonparticipating providers and facilities
scope: Nonparticipating (Out-of-Network) Providers and Facilities at Participating Facilities
key_principle: Establishes strict notice-and-consent requirements permitting certain nonparticipating providers to balance-bill patients for non-emergency services at participating facilities. Does not apply to in-network participating providers and cannot be used as a generic waiver to bypass plan prior-authorization requirements or shift contractual write-offs to patients.

title: Special rules for ambulance services, emergency and urgently needed services, and maintenance and post-stabilization care services
scope: Medicare Advantage (Part C) Plans
key_principle: Medicare Advantage organizations are prohibited under 42 CFR § 422.113(b)(2) from requiring prior authorization for emergency or urgently needed services, and member cost-sharing for emergency care cannot exceed Original Medicare levels. The federal No Surprises Act does not apply to Medicare Advantage.

title: Time frame for filing a request for a redetermination
scope: Original Medicare Fee-for-Service (Part A and Part B)
key_principle: A request for a redetermination must be filed within 120 calendar days from the date of receipt of the notice of initial determination. The date of receipt is legally presumed to be 5 calendar days after the date on the notice unless there is evidence showing otherwise.

title: 835 BPR16 Check Issue or EFT Effective Date Definition
scope: Electronic Remittance Advice (835) BPR Segment
key_principle: BPR16 represents the date payment was ordered/sent (check date or EFT effective date), not the claim adjudication date or formal denial notice date. It does not universally trigger provider appeal deadlines, which run from receipt of the initial determination or adverse benefit notice under program-specific rules.

citation: CMS Hospital Outpatient Department (OPD) Prior Authorization Operational Guide
title: Hospital Outpatient Department (OPD) Prior Authorization Process Operational Guide
scope: Original Medicare Fee-for-Service Hospital Outpatient Departments
key_principle: Prior authorization provisional affirmations issued by Medicare Administrative Contractors (MACs) under the OPD Prior Authorization program are generally valid for 120 calendar days from the date of the affirmation decision. Prior authorization validity periods are program- and payer-specific, not uniform across healthcare.

title: Request for a standard reconsideration
scope: Medicare Advantage (Part C) Organization Determinations
key_principle: An enrollee, appointed representative, or noncontracted provider (with a Waiver of Liability) may file a standard reconsideration request within 60 calendar days after the date of receipt of the written organization determination notice. Receipt is legally presumed to occur 5 calendar days after the notice date unless evidence shows otherwise. Contracted in-network providers follow contractual provider dispute resolution processes.

title: Claims procedure for employee benefit plans
scope: ERISA Covered Group Health Plans
key_principle: Establishes a minimum of 180 calendar days for a covered claimant to appeal an adverse benefit determination under group health plan rules. An assignment of benefits alone does not universally designate a provider as an authorized representative; provider representation depends on assignment terms, plan authorized-representative procedures (29 CFR § 2560.503-1(b)(4)), plan provisions, and governing law. It does not establish a universal deadline for an in-network provider's independent contractual claim dispute, which is governed by provider network agreements and state prompt-pay rules.

authority: U.S. Department of Labor (DOL) Employee Benefits Security Administration (EBSA)
citation: DOL EBSA Benefit Claims Procedure Regulation FAQs (29 CFR § 2560.503-1(b)(4))
title: Benefit Claims Procedure Regulation FAQs
scope: ERISA Covered Group Health Plans and Authorized Representatives
key_principle: An assignment of benefits (AOB) alone does not universally designate a healthcare provider as an authorized representative entitled to pursue an administrative appeal on the claimant's behalf under 29 CFR § 2560.503-1. Whether a provider may represent a claimant depends on the specific assignment terms, the plan's authorized-representative procedures established pursuant to § 2560.503-1(b)(4), plan terms (including valid anti-assignment clauses), and governing law.
